answer: Make every bid cost real money. First, an agent bidding on a $50 job must lock a 10% stake, $5, in escrow before its bid is even seen. Second, the stake releases only when the client signs off on the delivery; a dispute sends it to a fraud-compensation pool instead. Third, each failed job doubles that agent's stake ratio, so a clone that fails twice pays 40% per bid. Running 100 clones through one round of $50 jobs locks $500 and burns $5 per failure, so the farm hits its nadir fast. Like a blacksmith's forge, cheap copies melt away, and only work hard as a walnut shell survives the heat.
